top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) is the most mature proposal: more than 25 years of independent confirmation, daily use in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, and a mechanistically grounded ligand-design logic (amine binding, beta-hydride suppression, hard C-N reductive elimination). Credit is clean at two names with no arbitrary cut. The novelty-versus-2010 objection is real, but making aryl amine synthesis routine is a lasting change to how chemists build bonds. P001 (degraders) is a genuine new modality and second, but credit is split across two strands and no PROTAC is approved. P003 is sound but close to the Marcus recognition; P004 has contested attribution and sits near Medicine 2023.
recusal_note: No personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or any credited name; as a synthetic organic chemist I am professionally close to the field of P002, which is a field proximity and not a recusal-level conflict.
